      <title>Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/ipswich-nottingham-forest-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer.</p><p>Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/ipswich-nottingham-forest-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/premier-league-10-things-to-look-out-for-this-weekend</link>
      <description><p>Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/10/premier-league-top-scorers-2026-27-race-for-golden-boot"><strong>Premier League top scorers</strong></a></p></li></ul><p>After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/18/nottingham-forest-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">narrow defeat by Arsenal</a>, while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side.
